title: Introduction To Patient Care Procedures
description: Introduction to patient care procedures. Includes suctioning, artificial airways, tracheostomy, bronchoscopy, administration of hyperinflation therapy, airway pharmacology, bronchial hygiene therapy, aerosol drug therapy, non-invasive ventilation, basic and advanced airway care, and nutrition assessment. Intended for students in the Respiratory Therapy Program; enrollment is limited to students accepted in the program.
outcomes: Explain the indications, contraindications and hazards for invasive and noninvasive respiratory procedures administered.
The student will be able to demonstrate both invasive and noninvasive respiratory procedures as lab competencies, and must complete all lab competencies with a score of 70% or higher.
objectives: Describe how to safely perform endotracheal and nasotracheal suctioning
Assess the need for and select an artificial airway
Identify indications for a tracheostomy and bronchoscopy procedure
Demonstrate how to perform hyperinflation therapy
Demonstrate how to perform bronchial hygiene and chest physiotherapy
Describe the aerosol drug therapy and medications used for airway pharmacology
Describe the indications for non-invasive ventilation
Identify indications, complications, and hazards for arterial blood sampling
Discuss the effects of nutrition on the body from a respiratory standpoint
